title: Monotonicity of communication complexity in the error tolerance
statement: Fix a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and real error tolerances $\varepsilon', \varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$ is at most its $\varepsilon'$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity, where each such complexity is the infimum (in $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$) of the bit cost over all coin-tape lengths $n$ and all one-way public-coin protocols that compute $f$ to the corresponding error tolerance. In other words, relaxing the permitted error can only decrease (or leave unchanged) the required communication.
hypotheses_covered: a function f : X → Y → α
replaced:
The $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$ is
monotone non-increasing in $\varepsilon$: if $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$ then
$\mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon) \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon')$.  Intuitively, a
stricter error budget can only demand a larger protocol cost.
